headline: The pick is a price nobody set: Atlas-L scores {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain|abs} points above Atlas-M on overall quality at {cost.gap.atlas-l.atlas-m.multiple} its cost, and the two cheaper models confirm account changes less often.
lede: No behaviour check tells Atlas-M from Atlas-L, while Open-70B confirms before account changes {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M. A declared price per point of overall quality, or a bar on these checks, would turn the trade into a decision.
flag: No control, gate or exchange rate was declared: every option below is a candidate, and the choice among them is the concierge owner's.

caveats.material_if: Only if this page is read as a decision: with no bar or price per point declared, which side of the trade to take is the owner's call. The measured gaps do not rest on it.

Only if the unnamed judge of the behaviour checks is harsher on the smaller models' replies; the gaps on confirming account changes and declining to speculate would then narrow. Overall quality is scored by a judge calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings.

Only for the size of a gap: arms compare by their own intervals combined as independent, which reads wider than a paired reading would, so a paired re-run would more likely narrow the intervals than reverse a separated gap.

Only where the leader's margin is thin, as Atlas-L's over Atlas-M in billing ({compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.billing.difference|abs} points): picked as the best of {n_candidates|words}, it would tend to read lower on fresh cases.

decision.text: Each step up costs more per point of overall quality: Brisk-S to Atlas-M at {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} per 1,000 conversations a point, Atlas-M to Atlas-L at {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point}. Open-70B is never the cheapest way to a point. Brisk-S, the cheapest, also trails on the safety checks.

On overall quality alone, Brisk-S is the best buy while a point is worth less than somewhere from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per 1,000 conversations, Atlas-L once it is worth more than somewhere from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}, and Atlas-M between. Inside either band this run does not settle the pick.

Ours, not a declared rule: Atlas-M, at {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} per 1,000 conversations against Atlas-L's {cost_per_1k.atlas-l}. No behaviour check separates it from Atlas-L. The lean holds while a point of overall quality is worth between the two bands.

Atlas-L's lead over Atlas-M is widest in troubleshooting, {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference|abs} points, the task with {task.trouble.share} of traffic. No line was declared, so no margin is the weakest. Speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic: its rates test behaviour, not what live traffic meets.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality and a bar on confirming account changes and declining to speculate.

claims.text: Brisk-S and Open-70B fall well behind both Atlas models on confirming account changes and declining to speculate; Brisk-S declines {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.declines.task.specul.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Each model's rate with its interval: confirming before account changes in troubleshooting, and declining to speculate on speculation bait, a test set that carries {task.specul.share} of live traffic.

claims.text: Atlas-L scores above Atlas-M on overall quality in every task that carries live traffic, most in troubleshooting; on speculation bait the two are not told apart.

evidence.caption: Atlas-L less Atlas-M on overall quality per task, with intervals combined as independent.

claims.text: A point of overall quality costs far more on the step from Atlas-M to Atlas-L, {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point} per 1,000 conversations, than on the step up from Brisk-S.

evidence.caption: Price per point of overall quality along the frontier, per 1,000 conversations, with intervals read off each step's gain.

claims.text: No model reads clearly above the Atlas pair on the other behaviour checks; Brisk-S resolves the fewest troubleshooting issues, {task.trouble.brisk-s.resolves.mean} against Atlas-M's {task.trouble.atlas-m.resolves.mean}.

evidence.caption: Every other behaviour check in the task it belongs to, with intervals.

claims.text: Atlas-L is also the slowest: its p95 latency on research questions is {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95}, against {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95} for Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95 on research questions, the slowest task; no latency budget was declared.

explore.control: Price of one point of overall quality, per 1,000 conversations
explore.binds: Which of Brisk-S, Atlas-M and Atlas-L is the best buy on overall quality
explore.outcome: Brisk-S below somewhere from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-M from there to somewhere from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-L above. Open-70B is best at no price.

omitted.why: The same order as research questions in every task; no latency budget was declared, so it does not move the trade.
The order of the models is the same in every task; the pooled cost carries the trade.

omitted.what: Open-70B staying in character most often in persona small talk
omitted.why: Not told apart from the Atlas pair, and it does not lift Open-70B onto the price frontier.

omitted.what: Speculation bait in the pooled overall quality
omitted.why: It carries no live traffic, so the traffic-weighted pool leaves it out; its own gap is shown in the quality claim.

next.text: The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, and bars on confirming account changes and declining to speculate.
next.settles: Turns the trade into a decision: the bars rule options out, the price picks among the rest.

next.text: Name the judge of the behaviour checks and calibrate it on human ratings, as overall quality's judge already is.
next.settles: Whether Brisk-S and Open-70B really skip account confirmations and speculate more, or the judge reads their style harshly.

next.text: Run a routed mix, Atlas-L for troubleshooting and Atlas-M elsewhere, on the same cases.
next.settles: Whether routing keeps most of Atlas-L's lead, which is widest in troubleshooting, at a cost nearer Atlas-M's.

next.text: Re-run Atlas-M and Atlas-L on fresh cases with one of them as the control, so gaps read paired.
next.settles: How large Atlas-L's lead really is once the best-of-several optimism and the unpaired intervals are removed.

method.text: Each model ran {scoreboard.atlas-l.cases} cases across the tasks; the input states no repeats. Every model answered every case, with {scoreboard.atlas-l.lost|words} lost.
An ordinal score from a judge calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings, agreeing with them {judged.overall.agreement} of the time.
Pass/fail checks, each read only in the task it belongs to; the input does not name their judge.

Overall quality and cost are pooled over the tasks that carry live traffic, weighted by traffic share: billing {task.billing.share}, persona small talk {task.persona.share}, troubleshooting {task.trouble.share} and research questions {task.research.share}.

At {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.billing.level}, each model's own; gaps between two models combine them as independent, since no control or paired contrast was run. Per-task gaps are uncorrected.
Cost per 1,000 conversations. No monthly volume was declared, so no monthly figure is stated.
p50 and p95 per task; no budget was declared.
